description: Key facts a correct lesson on each Electromagnetic Theory topic must state. Every fact was taken from the fetched text of the source page named with it (the quote is checked by `npm run golden:check`). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the lesson text after LaTeX backslashes and braces are removed.
subject: em-theory

facts.claim: Telegrapher's equations: coupled PDEs for voltage and current on a line

source.quote: The telegrapher's equations (or telegraph equations) are a set of two coupled, linear partial differential equations

facts.claim: They let lines be analysed with circuit theory

source.quote: The equations are important because they allow transmission lines to be analyzed using circuit theory

facts.claim: SWR depends only on the magnitude of the reflection coefficient

source.quote: The standing wave ratio (SWR) is determined solely by the magnitude of the reflection coefficient

facts.claim: Graphical tool for transmission-line and matching problems

source.quote: The Smith chart is a circular nomogram used in radio frequency (RF) engineering to solve transmission line and impedance-matching problems

facts.claim: Wavelength scale for distance; degree scale for reflection phase

source.quote: The wavelength scale measures distance along a transmission line

facts.claim: A matched line has no reflections

source.quote: Signals on a transmission line will be transmitted without reflections if the transmission line is terminated with a matching impedance

facts.claim: Matching maximises power transfer

source.quote: the desired value is selected to maximize power transfer or minimize signal reflection

facts.claim: Describe how charges and currents create electric and magnetic fields

source.quote: describe how electric and magnetic fields are generated by electric charges and currents

facts.claim: Gauss, Gauss for magnetism, Faraday, Ampère–Maxwell

source.quote: Gauss's law, Gauss's law for magnetism, Faraday's law, Ampère-Maxwe

facts.claim: Tangential E is continuous across the interface

source.quote: the tangential component of E is continuous across the interface

facts.claim: Tangential H jumps by the surface current density

source.quote: the tangential component of H is discontinuous across the interface by an amount equal to the magnitude of the surface current density

facts.claim: Polarisation is the orientation of oscillation in transverse waves

source.quote: is a property of transverse waves which specifies the geometrical orientation of the oscillations

facts.claim: Oscillation is perpendicular to travel

source.quote: the direction of the oscillation is perpendicular to the direction of motion of the wave

facts.claim: AC current crowds near the surface (skin effect)

source.quote: the current density is largest near the surfac

facts.claim: Higher frequency → smaller skin depth

source.quote: as frequency increases, current flow becomes more concentrated near the surface, resulting in less skin depth

facts.claim: Poynting vector = directional energy flux (power per area)

source.quote: represents the directional energy flux (the energy transfer per unit area, per unit time)

facts.claim: Unit W/m²

source.quote: The SI unit of the Poynting vector is the watt per square metre

facts.claim: Each mode has a cutoff frequency below which it won't propagate

source.quote: each mode had a cutoff frequency below which waves would not propagate

facts.claim: TE and TM modes

source.quote: either the electric field (TE modes) or magnetic field (TM modes)

facts.claim: The same pattern for transmit and receive (reciprocity)

source.quote: the same radiation pattern applies both to transmission as well as reception of radio waves

facts.claim: Omnidirectional versus directional antennas

source.quote: Antennas can be classified as omnidirectional, radiating energy approximately equally in all horizontal directions, or directional

facts.claim: A dipole has two identical conductors

source.quote: a dipole antenna which consists of two identical rod conductors

facts.claim: A monopole is one rod over a ground plane

source.quote: a straight rod-shaped conductor, often mounted perpendicularly over some type of conductive surface, called a ground plane
